approachQuestion.prompt:
Move the Closing Segment

A finite acyclic singly linked list contains n records. Move the last k records to the front, preserving their order and that of the other records; repeating beyond n wraps around. Return the same node objects with unchanged values and a null-terminated result. Only next links may change. Input is head and integer k, 0 <= k <= 10^18 and 0 <= n <= 200000. Arithmetic on these integers is constant-time and exact.

Input: [6,8,2,9,4], k=7. Output: [9,4,6,8,2].
Input: null, k=12. Output: null. Input: [5], k=0. Output: the same node.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Normalize k, then reverse the whole list.
options.feedback: For [1,2,3] and k=1 reversal gives [3,2,1] rather than [3,1,2].

options.text: Normalize k and join tail to head, returning the start of the rotated suffix without cutting any link.
options.feedback: For any nonempty input with a nonzero remainder this leaves a cycle instead of the required null-terminated result.

options.text: If empty return null. Count nodes and find the tail; reduce k modulo n. If the remainder is zero return head. Otherwise join tail to head, advance to the node n-remainder-1 links from head, save its successor as new head, and cut its next to null.
options.feedback: The normalized remainder determines the suffix size, and the cut restores a finite list at precisely the new boundary.

options.text: Store all node references in an array, normalize k by the array length (handling empty input), then relink them in rotated array-index order.
options.feedback: This returns the correct rotation but stores avoidable node references.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-10-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Counting and locating the cut each traverse at most n links; a nonempty long list requires counting even for a large k. Modulo is one word operation. Fixed references and counters suffice, and there is no iteration proportional to k or recursion.
